protocol.copyright: Copyright 2026 BifrOSt. Private protocol of the BifrOSt window server (docs/window-server.md, "Window capture").

interface.name: bifrost_window_capture_manager_v1
interface.description:
Lets the shell take a scaled-down picture of one toplevel, for Mission Control tiles, the Dock's thumbnails of minimized windows and window screenshots. A picture shows the window alone (its surface tree, material regions as flat plates) on a transparent ground: nothing that overlaps the window on the screen is in it, and a window the window server holds minimized can still be captured.
This global is offered to the shell only. The window server hides it from every other client (it is not listed in their registry) and refuses a request from one that bound it anyway with `failed(denied)`.
A capture is on demand and one-shot: the request carries the buffer to fill and the answer is one event on the frame object. The window server fits the window into the buffer, keeping its aspect and never scaling it up, so the buffer's size is the largest picture wanted. The picture is written from the buffer's top-left corner, `width` by `height` pixels, rows `stride` bytes apart; the rest of the buffer is not touched.

request.name: capture_surface

description.summary: capture the toplevel of a surface

request.description: Captures the toplevel whose root surface is `surface`: a window of the requesting client. `buffer` is a wl_shm buffer in argb8888 or xrgb8888 (argb8888 keeps the transparent corners); its premultiplied pixels are in the shm convention. `since` is the serial of the last picture the client holds of this window at this buffer size, or 0 for none: when the window has not changed since, `unchanged` is sent and nothing is drawn.

request.name: capture_toplevel

description.summary: capture a toplevel of any client

request.description: Captures the window of a foreign toplevel handle the requesting client holds (wlr-foreign-toplevel): the way to name a window of another client, whose surface the shell never sees. Otherwise as `capture_surface`.

interface.name: bifrost_window_capture_frame_v1

description.summary: the answer to one capture request

interface.description: Exactly one of `ready`, `unchanged` and `failed` is sent, once, right after the request that created the object. The object stays valid until it is destroyed.

event.name: ready

description.summary: the picture is in the buffer

event.description: The window, scaled to `width` by `height` pixels, is in the top-left corner of the buffer. `serial` names this picture: pass it as `since` to ask whether the window changed after it.

event.name: unchanged

description.summary: the window did not change since the picture the client holds

event.description: The window has not committed new content since `serial`; the buffer was not written.

entry.name: unsupported
entry.summary: the window server has no renderer that can capture a window

entry.name: gone
entry.summary: no such window, or it has no content

entry.name: bad_buffer
entry.summary: not a wl_shm buffer in argb8888 or xrgb8888, or its rows are short

entry.name: denied
entry.summary: the requesting client is not the shell
